chapter: Western University and Kansas City nightlife
title: Leaving Austin in 1932 for Western University and working his way through
summary: He left August 1932 on a music scholarship to Western University in Kansas, working odd jobs and painting buildings.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Oh, you left in '32 to go to college? Wheatland?
Yeah, I left August 18, 1932, to go to Western University in Quindare (phonetic), Kansas. This is a suburb of Kansas City, Missouri. I think our band just about folded up then.
Now, under what circumstances did you go to this college?
Well, I kinda' had a musical scholarship.
Yeah. I had to work my way through, too.
And I was--I left out my basic learnings in Texas and everything.
Well, put that in now, then.
'Course, I used to pick turkeys, too; I used to pick cotton, pick turkeys, shine shoes with a little box on the streets, you know.
Dirty cowboy shoes. I worked as a dishwasher, different jobs, but, uh--
This would be probably in the summer vacations?

Yeah. But I had an uncle named Calvin who was a painter by trade, house painter by trade. He had taught me painting. So when I got to Western University, a friend of mine, Emmett Lindsay and I, not only did we take over the furnace room and handle those big boilers (in the) boiler room, but we also painted the whole seven buildings on the outside. Everybody else was afraid of those scaffolds, you know. Three stories high. And we'd get up there and do the whole thing, paint the windows and everything.
Oh. So this sorta' kept you in feathers (phonetic) funds.
